topics.topic: Ownership of enforcing Linux runtime and filesystem prerequisites before deployment
questions: Which module or external route owns the Linux-only deployment constraint and decides whether a target environment is eligible to run the service?
Which module or external route owns establishing the required Linux runtime and filesystem semantics before the service starts?

quotes:
The service runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named (owner, 2026-11-21). Another
   system, or a Linux or file system on which a call these rules rely on — opening without following a
   link, opening a folder as a folder, opening without blocking, creating exclusively, locking, renaming,
   flushing — does not act as Linux documents it, is unsupported: the service neither tests for it nor
   defines what it does there.
judgement.divergence: The deployment route rejects a target lacking the required Linux filesystem semantics before startup, or it deploys without checking and the service reaches undefined behavior when it uses those semantics; the deployer, service operator and calling flow notice the difference.
judgement.why: The Linux-only constraint affects observable deployment eligibility, but State 3 assigns neither a service module nor the external deployment route ownership of enforcing it.

witness.initial: A deployment targets Linux on a file system whose locking does not act as Linux documents it.
events: the deployment route checks the distributions installed in the image before deployment
the deployment route decides whether to deploy the image
the calling flow asks the deployed service to deliver one photo, causing the project lock to be used
outcomes: the deployment route rejects the target before the service starts because the required Linux filesystem semantics are not present
the deployment proceeds because no owner checks the prerequisite, and behavior is undefined when the service takes the project lock
witness.observer: the deployer, service operator and calling flow
basis:
Before each deployment every distribution installed
   in the image is checked against a snapshot of the OSV database, ecosystem PyPI, that the deployment route accepts
   as current.

The deliverer offers three operations: scan a project's folder, deliver one photo, and record its
publication.

Deliveries and marks of one project run one at a time, across processes, under an operating
   system lock on one lock file of that project in the state folder.

topics.topic: Minimum supported Linux kernel/libc version and compatibility policy
questions: Does this require compatibility with every Linux version whose filesystem supplies the listed semantics, permit the implementation to choose a minimum kernel or libc version through its system calls, or defer the supported version to the deployment image?

quotes:
The service runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named (owner, 2026-11-21). Another
   system, or a Linux or file system on which a call these rules rely on — opening without following a
   link, opening a folder as a folder, opening without blocking, creating exclusively, locking, renaming,
   flushing — does not act as Linux documents it, is unsupported: the service neither tests for it nor
   defines what it does there.
judgement.why: Support is defined by Linux behavior of the relied-on calls rather than by a kernel or libc version, and the service neither probes nor defines behavior when those semantics are unavailable.
